title: SensorLab Analytics
tagline: Reproducible Data Analysis & ML Sensitivity Prediction for Flexible Capacitive Pressure Sensors
description: A reproducible scientific data-analysis and predictive workflow for flexible capacitive pressure sensors. Automates the ingestion of raw LCR meter experimental CSV files, extraction of capacitance–pressure curves, sensitivity slope calculation (S = δ(ΔC/C₀)/δP), Scikit-learn regression models for sensitivity prediction from nanofiller loading, hysteresis evaluation, response/recovery time kinetics (τ_r, τ_d), and generation of publication-quality plots.
workflow: Raw LCR CSV Data Ingestion → Baseline Drift Correction (Polynomial Filter) → Capacitance–Pressure Response Extraction → Sensitivity Slope Regression → Scikit-learn Sensitivity Modeling → Dynamic Hysteresis Quantitation → Publication-Grade Matplotlib Figures.
features: Automated experimental CSV parsing with standardized instrument headers.
Capacitance–pressure response curve plotting with error bars.
Piecewise linear sensitivity calculation across low-pressure (0–1.5 kPa) and extended ranges.
Materials Science ML: Scikit-learn regression models to predict sensitivity from filler loading (wt% TiO₂, ZnO, CB).
Dynamic hysteresis loop calculation and percent error quantification.
Step-response and relaxation time constant extraction (τ_r, τ_d < 38 ms).
Sensor batch performance comparison across varying nanocomposite formulations.
Self-contained, reproducible Jupyter Notebook outputs for laboratory documentation.

title: AI-Assisted Sensor Research
tagline: Practical AI-Assisted Scientific Programming & Reproducible Workflows
description: A structured research workflow demonstrating how modern AI coding assistants (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and Google Antigravity) support scientific Python development for sensor researchers. Demonstrates prompt engineering for materials science, custom instruction files, automated test generation, and strict human review of generated code.
workflow: Research Hypothesis → AI-Assisted Script Scaffolding → Scientific Code Review & Inspection → Domain Validation Rules (SKILL.md) → Automated pytest Generation → Git Version Control.
features: AI-assisted notebook creation and script generation for sensor electromechanics.
Reusable scientific instructions and prompt templates for materials calculations.
Domain-specific SKILL.md files (sensor-data-analysis, scientific-report-writing).
Automated code checks, docstring generation, and regression tests with pytest.
Systematic debugging and refactoring of experimental analysis notebooks.
Strict human-in-the-loop review ensuring physical realism and mathematical validity.
Version-controlled scientific repository maintenance following Git best practices.

title: Scientific Literature & Research Workflow
tagline: Evidence-Backed Literature Synthesis & Structured Metric Extraction
description: An AI-assisted scientific literature review workflow utilizing existing research tools and integrations to streamline literature discovery, DOI-based verification, and structured extraction of reported sensor performance metrics (permittivity, sensitivity, linearity, hysteresis) with mandatory source verification.
workflow: Scholarly Literature Lookup (Crossref/OpenAlex) → PDF Metadata Parsing → Structured Property Extraction Table → Mandatory DOI Attribution Verification → Reference Management Organization.
features: DOI-based scholarly lookup and citation metadata extraction.
Structured paper comparison across polymer matrix formulations (PDMS, PVDF, PU).
Extraction of reported nanofiller fractions (TiO₂, ZnO, CB) and sensitivity metrics.
Evidence verification against original published manuscripts (eliminates hallucinations).
Identification of materials processing conditions (sonication time, curing temperatures).
Drafting transparent research summaries with explicit human verification.
Integration with existing reference management workflows (e.g. Zotero/BibTeX).
